not: A ceremony framework: every mechanism must prevent a real failure worth its cost.
A second source of truth beside Git.
An engine that invents human decisions or acts without authority.
A deploy, CI or release-publishing tool: its release support is a branching strategy.
Inherently opinionated: it ships an opinionated default graph, but every opinion (graph, lenses, prompts, policy) can be customised by the project.
principles: Git is the store; state is visible and repairable by hand.
A small engine; the graph, prompts and policy belong to the project.
Human authority is explicit: approvals may be delegated, but decisions with big consequences go to the owner, batched.
Reviews are independent, and a finding must matter.

Guard against drift at both levels: from what a goal asked for, and from the project's original intent. A goal that departs from the project's intent is flagged when it is added, and the owner either changes the goal or amends the intent.
Prefer deleting to adding; keep prompts distilled.
intent.purpose: Let coding agents carry long-running repository work through durable, reviewable goals, so a developer can stop supervising without losing progress, priorities or control.
intent.serves: Developers who delegate project work to coding agents, and the agents doing it.

spec:
After real publication, mechanically update ONLY the Implementation note in docs/WHITEPAPER.md to identify the actual published semantic version, tag and immutable commit, with verified matching package build and source/reference links. Replace development-only wording accurately. Preserve all conceptual prose, Prior Work, existing exact-term acknowledgement, byline and the decision to have no blog. Do not alter runtime, policy, templates, schemas, contracts, release-2 goals, release/main branches or publication machinery. The source PR targets dev through existing repository policy; root separately handles any reviewed carry to main.

Root procedural gate: discovery, routine approvals, base and test-review preparation may proceed now, but the coordinator MUST NOT claim/start implement or write any release pin until root supplies the actual published tag/commit/asset receipt. Preview or predicted versions do not satisfy this gate. No release is asserted as published by creating this goal. Receipt metadata is dynamic execution evidence; do not rewrite the spec or stale phases simply when it arrives.

At implement, retrieve and verify actual public release/tag/commit metadata and matching package-build/source facts, using root's publication receipt as the starting evidence. Persist the authoritative URLs, commit/version/build and verification result in phase output. If publication is absent or facts disagree, do not write an unverified pin; report the concrete missing evidence. The pin must name what actually published, never a guessed or preview version.

This is a tiny mechanical documentation follow-up to closed goals 1036 and 1045, release 1/P1. Use a very short adoption design and proportionate independent reviews; reuse the existing Git whitespace goal command and unchanged configured repository verification, with no new tests, checkers, research or infrastructure. Keep ordinary phase and exact-head checks. Routine approvals use the standing exact quote "Do not wait for my approval", decided_by "Codex (root agent), delegated by Dave". Source PR merges remain with root; the user's explicit "Use admin merge" authority may be applied by root only after verified current required checks and exact head. This goal neither publishes a release nor claims a predicted version is published.
title: pin whitepaper implementation note to the published release
